It records recovery timing, initial and discharge pain scores, nausea or vomiting, ambulation and oral-intake timing, urinary and drain output, wound assessment, infection signs, temperature, transfusions, ICU transfers, complications, length of stay, discharge destination, assessment date, and a calculated 30-day readmission risk score. `first_ambulation_hours` can be `NULL` when ambulation is not applicable, and `drain_output_ml` can be `NULL` when no surgical drain was placed.

The data can be used to examine recovery patterns and outcomes, such as time in PACU or hospital, changes in pain scores, rates of complications or ICU transfers, and discharge destinations. It can also support comparisons of recovery measures with readmission risk, or analyses of recorded wound and infection findings, transfusions, and post-operative symptoms.
mental_healths_large.feedbackactionitems:
The `mental_healths_large.FeedbackActionItems` table contains records of actions created in response to patient feedback surveys. Each record includes a survey reference, action category, responsible department, priority, and resolution status. It also tracks assignment and resolution times, escalation, patient contact attempts and outcomes, root-cause analysis, systemic issues, recommended policy changes, staff training, service-recovery costs, recent similar complaints, creation date, and follow-up survey status. A `NULL` value for `days_to_resolution` indicates that the action item is still open.

The table can be used to analyze action-item volume and status by category, priority, or department; compare assignment and resolution times; identify open, escalated, or unresolvable items; and examine how often actions involve systemic issues, policy changes, or training. It can also support analysis of patient-contact outcomes, service-recovery costs, complaint patterns over time, and whether follow-up surveys are sent after resolution.
mental_healths_large.clinicalpathwayadhe:
The `mental_healths_large.ClinicalPathwayAdherence` table contains one record per clinical pathway adherence assessment, linked to a patient encounter. Records identify the pathway and protocol version and include pathway steps completed, adherence percentage, whether critical steps were met, and variance counts and reasons.

The table also records time to first intervention, expected and actual length of stay and cost, whether the expected outcome was achieved, 30-day readmission status, quality score, and assessment date.

The data can be used to compare adherence and outcomes across pathways or protocol versions, examine common variance reasons, assess differences between expected and actual length of stay or cost, and analyze how intervention timing relates to outcomes, readmissions, or quality scores. It can also support tracking these measures over time.
museum_artifact_large.insurancepolicies:
The `InsurancePolicies` table contains insurance policy identifiers, provider names, policy types, coverage periods, active-status flags, and links to loans or exhibitions. Its policy types include Exhibition, General Collection, Incoming Loan, and Outgoing Loan. The `policy_financials` field stores JSON financial details in USD, including total coverage value, annual premium, and deductible. The table also records who updated each policy.

The data can be used to identify active or expired policies, review coverage by policy type, provider, loan, or exhibition, and examine policy start and end dates. Financial analysis could compare coverage values, premiums, and deductibles across policies or providers.
museum_artifact_large.lendinginstitution:
The `museum_artifact_large.LendingInstitutions` table contains records for lending institutions. It includes each institution’s registry number, name, type, primary contact details, website, accreditation, partnership level, security description, record creation timestamp, and shipping address stored as JSON.

The table can be used to find institutions by registry number or name, group or compare institutions by type, accreditation, or partnership level, retrieve contact and shipping information, and review recorded security details. The creation timestamp can support analysis of when institution records were added.
museum_artifact_large.artifactprovenance:
The `museum_artifact_large.ArtifactProvenance` table contains provenance and ownership records linked to artifacts through `artifact_history_for`. Fields cover previous owners and collections, owner type, provenance narratives, country of origin, legal status, authenticity scores, verification dates and staff codes, public visibility, record creation timestamps, and acquisition details such as method, date, and price.

The table can support questions about an artifact’s recorded ownership history, origin, acquisition, legal status, and authenticity assessment. It can also be used to analyze the distribution of records by country of origin, owner type, legal status, or collection; identify records with unverified or unresolved titles; and track verification and record-creation timelines.
museum_artifact_large.airqualityreadings:
`museum_artifact_large.AirQualityReadings` stores air-quality sensor snapshots. Each row has a unique `aq_id`, an `env_link` referencing `EnvironmentalReadingsCore.monitor_code`, and an `air_quality_metrics` JSONB value containing gaseous-pollutant and particulate measurements.

The data can be used to inspect pollutant measurements by snapshot, compare measurements across readings, and join air-quality data to related environmental readings for combined analysis.
museum_artifact_large.artifactscore:
The `museum_artifact_large.ArtifactsCore` table contains artifact records identified by the unique `ARTregID`. Each record may include a title, dynasty or period, age in years, material type, and conservation status. A `NULL` title or conservation status means that information was not provided.

The table can be used to look up artifacts by ID; count or compare artifacts by dynasty, material, or conservation status; examine age distributions across those categories; and identify records with missing titles or conservation-status information.
museum_artifact_large.riskassessments:
The `museum_artifact_large.RiskAssessments` table records risk assessments associated with artifacts or exhibition halls. Each record has a unique `risk_id` and references an artifact through `art_concern`, a hall through `hall_concern`, or both. It includes the risk level, emergency-plan status, evacuation priority, handling rules, and a conservation score.

The table can be used to identify artifacts or halls by risk level, review emergency-plan and evacuation-priority statuses, compare handling requirements, and examine conservation scores across assessed items or halls.
museum_artifact_large.artifactsecurityac:
The `museum_artifact_large.ArtifactSecurityAccess` table contains artifact loan status, insurance value in USD, security level, access restrictions, research access status, and documentation and conservation statuses. Its fields include loan status, security level, access restriction, documentation status, photo documentation status, condition report status, conservation recommendations, research access, and digital record status.

The table can be used to examine how artifacts are distributed across loan, security, and access categories; compare insurance values by security level or loan status; identify artifacts with documentation or condition reports due; and review conservation recommendations or digital record completion status.
museum_artifact_large.artifactratings:
The `museum_artifact_large.ArtifactRatings` table stores ratings associated with artifacts. Each row has a unique historical identifier (`HIST_sign`), a reference to an artifact through `ART_link`, and a JSONB payload (`rating_profile`) that groups curatorial and conservation-planning ratings, including significance, display priority, and treatment difficulty.

The table can be used to retrieve an artifact’s rating profile, compare ratings across artifacts, and analyze how significance, display priority, or treatment difficulty vary across the collection.
museum_artifact_large.sensitivitydata:
The `museum_artifact_large.SensitivityData` table links artifacts to environmental sensitivity identifiers and stores a JSON profile of factors relevant to preventive conservation.

- `ENVsense` is the primary key and has the possible values `High`, `Low`, and `Medium`.
- `ART_link` references `ArtifactsCore.ARTregID`.
- `env_handling_sensitivity` contains a multi-factor profile covering environmental conditions, pests, handling, transport, display, and storage.

The table can be used to look up an artifact’s recorded sensitivity profile, group linked artifacts by environmental sensitivity, and examine which conservation factors are represented in profiles. It can also support questions such as which artifacts have a given sensitivity identifier or which profiles include information about handling, transport, display, or storage.
museum_artifact_large.conservationandmai:
The `museum_artifact_large.ConservationAndMaintenance` table contains conservation and maintenance records identified by `maint_id`. Records can link to environmental readings through `monitor_link`, surface and physical readings through `surf_link`, and a previous treatment through `prevTreat`.

The table includes treatment and incident statuses, action priorities, cleaning dates and intervals, maintenance logs, drill and staff training statuses, budget allocation and availability, conservation frequency, treatment history, treatment effectiveness, and potential reversibility of damage.

The data can be used to identify cleaning that is due based on `lastClean`, `nextClean`, or `cleanDays`; review records by priority, treatment, or incident status; assess training and emergency-drill status; examine budget conditions; and analyze patterns in conservation frequency, treatment outcomes, or damage reversibility. Linked reading records can support analysis of maintenance actions alongside environmental and physical conditions.
museum_artifact_large.exhibitionhalls:
The `ExhibitionHalls` table contains one record per exhibition hall, identified by `Hall_ID`. Its `security_visitor_overview` JSONB field combines hall-level security system states with visitor statistics.

The data can be used to examine how visitor counts relate to security states, identify halls that may need staffing adjustments, and compare security and visitor patterns across halls. The JSONB field’s specific keys and measures are not described in the schema.
museum_artifact_large.publications:
The `museum_artifact_large.Publications` table contains publication records, including publication codes, titles, types, publication dates, publishers, identifiers (DOI and ISBN), researcher references, abstracts, keywords, language, and links to full text. It also records whether a publication is peer-reviewed, the exhibit it may relate to, and when the record was added.

The table can be used to find publications by type, date, publisher, language, or peer-review status; identify publications associated with a researcher or exhibition; and analyze publication counts and trends over time. Abstracts and keywords can support searches by subject, while DOI, ISBN, and full-text links can help locate publication records and their content.
museum_artifact_large.digitalassets:
The `museum_artifact_large.DigitalAssets` table stores metadata about digital assets associated with museum artifacts. Each record includes an asset registry tag, the related artifact identifier, asset type, file format and size, capture timestamp, technician reference, and storage URI. It also records licensing terms, public-access status, copyright owner, asset description, quality-control status, version, and an optional parent asset tag.

The table can be used to:
- List digital assets for an artifact or group them by asset type or file format.
- Analyze file sizes, capture dates, or assets recorded by technician.
- Find assets by storage location, licensing terms, access status, or copyright owner.
- Track quality-control status and distinguish versions or assets linked through parent tags.
museum_artifact_large.artists:
The `museum_artifact_large.Artists` table contains artist records with registry codes, names, birth and death dates, nationality, biographies, art movements, style schools, and primary dynasties. It also records whether an artist is anonymous, their primary medium and notable works, research notes, the staff reference associated with record creation, and the record creation timestamp.

The data can be used to answer questions such as how artists are distributed by nationality, dynasty, medium, or style school; which artists are recorded as anonymous; and what works or research notes are associated with an artist. It can also support analyses of artist lifespans where dates are available, and record-keeping activity by creator or creation date.
museum_artifact_large.artifactartistlink:
The `museum_artifact_large.ArtifactArtistLink` table records links between artworks and artists. Each row includes an artwork identifier, an artist identifier, attribution level and date, and whether the artist is marked as the primary creator. It can also contain the artist’s creation role, the verifying staff code, verification notes, a publication source, and a confidence score.

The table can be used to identify artists associated with an artwork, distinguish primary creators from other linked artists, and examine how attributions vary by date, level, role, or source. It can also support analysis of verification records and confidence scores across artwork–artist links.
museum_artifact_large.showcases:
The `Showcases` table records showcase identifiers, their associated exhibition halls, and a JSON profile of each showcase’s physical condition, filtration and adsorption capacity, leak performance, and safety-power states.

It can be used to link showcases to halls and analyze or monitor their reported environmental and operational states. For example, it can help answer which hall a showcase is in, or compare showcases by recorded leak performance, filtration capacity, or safety-power state.
museum_artifact_large.environmentalreadi:
`EnvironmentalReadingsCore` records environmental measurements for museum showcases. Each row is identified by `monitor_code`, includes a required reading timestamp (`readTS`), and may link to a showcase through `case_link`.

The recorded measurements include temperature in Celsius (`TEMPc`), 24-hour temperature variance (`tempVar24`), relative humidity (`RH`), humidity variance (`RHvar`), and air pressure (`air_press`). A `NULL` air-pressure value indicates that no air-pressure data is available.

The data can be used to examine environmental conditions by showcase or over time, compare temperature and humidity readings and their recorded variances, identify readings with missing air-pressure data, and explore how conditions change across monitoring periods.
museum_artifact_large.exhibitions:
The `museum_artifact_large.Exhibitions` table contains exhibition records, including catalog codes, titles, dates, themes, hall locations, and status. It also records the staff tag of the curator in charge, budget and actual cost, whether an exhibition is traveling, its sponsoring organization, a press-release link, and expected and actual attendance figures stored in JSON.

The table can be used to answer questions such as which exhibitions ran during a given period, who curated them, where they were held, and which were traveling. It can also support analysis of budget versus actual cost, attendance versus expectations, exhibition duration, and counts of exhibitions by status, location, curator, or sponsor.
museum_artifact_large.artifactconservato:
The `museum_artifact_large.ArtifactConservatorLink` table records conservation treatments associated with artifacts and conservator staff. It includes artifact and staff references, treatment type and dates, report and project references, whether a conservator was the lead, hours worked, materials used, and a treatment summary. It also records the authorization date and the authorizing staff reference.

The data can be used to answer questions such as which conservators worked on an artifact or project, what treatments were performed and when, how many hours were recorded, which conservators served as leads, and which materials were used. It can also support analysis of treatment activity by type, project, time period, or staff member.
museum_artifact_large.lightandradiationr:
The `museum_artifact_large.LightAndRadiationReadings` table stores light and radiation measurements. Each row has a unique `rad_id` and an `env_link` referencing an environmental reading through `EnvironmentalReadingsCore.monitor_code`. Measurements include light level in lux (`lux`), ultraviolet radiation in microwatts (`UV_uW`), infrared radiation in watts (`IR_W`), and visible-light exposure in lux-hours (`visLxh`). The measurement fields are extracted from the `radiation_exposure` JSON.

The table can be used to examine recorded light and radiation levels, compare measurements associated with environmental readings, and analyze visible-light exposure or UV and IR readings across records.
museum_artifact_large.surfaceandphysical:
`SurfaceAndPhysicalReadings` stores surface and physical measurements linked to environmental readings through `env_link`, with `surf_id` as the primary key. Its fields cover vibration, noise, dust, microbes, mold, pest activity and species, surface pH and moisture, salt risk, corrosion, organic degradation, color difference, temperature, humidity, structural condition, cracks, deformation, material weight percentage, and oxygen and nitrogen levels. It also records thermal-image status and condition-risk categories.

`NULL` in `pestActivity` means no pest activity was reported; `NULL` in `pestSpecies` means no species was identified. A `NULL` `thermalImg` or `structStable` value means that data was not provided.

The data can be used to examine surface conditions and potential damage indicators, compare readings across environmental records, identify patterns in pest or mold observations, and track measurements such as moisture, corrosion, deformation, or color difference.
museum_artifact_large.usagerecords:
The `museum_artifact_large.UsageRecords` table contains usage and care information for artifacts or exhibits. Each record has a unique `usage_id` and may link to an environmental reading through `env_link`. Fields describe rotation schedules, display and rest durations, display/storage/handling/transport/packing requirements, access and activity frequencies, and monitoring, assessment, conservation, maintenance, inspection, and calibration schedules. Status fields record certification, compliance, audit, and quality outcomes.

The table can be used to analyze display and rest schedules, compare care and handling requirements, review how frequently artifacts are accessed or maintained, and identify records with expired certifications, non-compliant status, failed audits, or quality issues. The environmental-reading link can support analysis of usage records alongside environmental data.
museum_artifact_large.monitor_showcase_m:
The `museum_artifact_large.Monitor_Showcase_Map` table records associations between monitors and showcase cases. Each row contains a `mon_ID` and a `case_ID`; together they form the primary key, and `case_ID` references `Showcases.caseID`.

The table can be used to identify which showcase cases are associated with a monitor, which monitors are associated with a case, and to count or analyze monitor–case associations.
museum_artifact_large.conditionassessmen:
The `ConditionAssessments` table records condition assessments, including a unique assessment ID, references to the artifact and showcase examined, a link to light and radiation readings, an assessment score, the assessment date, and the next due date.

The data can be used to identify assessments due by a given date, review assessment history for an artifact or showcase, analyze score changes over time, and examine how assessment scores relate to linked light and radiation readings.
museum_artifact_large.staff:
The `museum_artifact_large.Staff` table contains staff identification, employment, organizational, and contact information. It includes names and employee codes; job titles and departments; manager codes and office locations; start and end dates and employment status; and role indicators for curator, conservator, and researcher. It also records specialization, nationality, professional biographies, security clearance, system-user roles, and last-login timestamps.

Additional fields cover staff administration, including performance scores, review dates, remaining annual leave and sick days, payroll references, training records, and emergency contact details. The schema includes personal information such as dates of birth, home addresses, email addresses, and phone extensions.

The table can support questions and analysis such as:
- How many staff members are in each department or employment-status category?
- Which staff members report to a particular manager or hold particular job titles or role indicators?
- How long have staff members been employed, based on their start and end dates?
- Which staff members have upcoming reviews, or how do performance scores vary by department or role?
- How are training records, leave balances, and system roles distributed across staff?
museum_artifact_large.conservationtreatm:
The `museum_artifact_large.ConservationTreatments` table contains treatment work orders for museum artifacts. It records the artifact and requesting staff code, request date, reason and priority, proposed treatment plan, estimated duration, approval status and manager, treatment start and end dates, and links to final reports and post-treatment assessments.

The data can be used to track treatment requests from submission through completion, review approval and scheduling status, compare estimated treatment durations with timelines, and analyze treatment activity by priority, staff code, or date. It can also help identify artifacts awaiting approval or treatment and retrieve final reports and follow-up assessments.
museum_artifact_large.researchers:
The `museum_artifact_large.Researchers` table contains researcher identifiers, names, email addresses, institutional affiliations, positions, biographies, specialties, and ORCID identifiers. It also records whether each researcher is internal, a staff profile reference, their access level, access start and end dates, and profile creation timestamps.

The table can be used to answer questions such as how many researchers are associated with each institution or specialty, which researchers have a particular access level, and which access periods are currently active or have expired. It can also support analysis of researcher profiles by internal status, staff profile, institution, or profile creation date.
museum_artifact_large.artifactpublicatio:
The table records links between museum artifacts and publications. Each record identifies an artifact (`mentioned_artifact_tag`) and a publication (`in_publication_tag`), with optional page and figure references, a citation context, and a reference type such as “Illustrated,” “Discussed,” or “Catalogue Entry.” It also indicates whether the artifact is the publication’s primary subject and records a staff tag and link creation timestamp.

The table can be used to find publications associated with an artifact, identify artifacts covered by a publication, and retrieve the relevant pages, figures, and context. It can also support analysis of reference types, primary-subject status, and link creation dates.
museum_artifact_large.materialanalysis:
The `museum_artifact_large.MaterialAnalysis` table records material analyses associated with museum artifacts. It includes an analysis reference and artifact identifier, analysis date and method, laboratory and technician, purpose, and report code. Results-related fields include composition data in JSON format, density, and confidence level. The table also records whether an analysis is destructive, sample weight and location, analysis cost, and the next analysis due date.

The data can be used to:
- Review analyses and results for a specific artifact or date range.
- Compare analysis methods, laboratories, or reported compositions.
- Identify destructive analyses and summarize their sample weights and locations.
- Track analysis costs, confidence levels, and upcoming analysis due dates.
- Count or categorize analyses by purpose, method, or laboratory.
museum_artifact_large.transportationlog:
The `museum_artifact_large.TransportationLog` table contains transportation records associated with loans. Fields include shipment and manifest identifiers, transport company, shipment start and end times, origin and destination, transport mode, total weight, maximum recorded G-force and internal temperature, arrival-check result, damage or incident notes, and travel distance.

The data can be used to calculate shipment durations, compare travel distances and weights by route or transport mode, review arrival-check outcomes, and examine reported incidents alongside recorded G-force and temperature. It can also support summaries of shipments by loan, company, origin, destination, or time period.
museum_artifact_large.emergencyplans:
The `museum_artifact_large.EmergencyPlans` table contains emergency-plan records identified by protocol code, hall, and plan name. Each record can include an emergency type, activation protocol, primary responder staff ID, evacuation map, assembly point, artifact salvage list reference, last drill date, active status, and JSON metadata about the plan’s version, update, updater, and next scheduled review.

The table can be used to find plans for a specific hall or emergency type, review activation and evacuation instructions, identify the assigned responder and assembly point, check drill dates and plan status, and examine version or review information. It can also support analyses such as counts of plans by emergency type or hall, and checks for plans with missing or outdated drill or review information.
museum_artifact_large.artifactprofile:
`museum_artifact_large.ArtifactProfile` stores artifact profile records, each identified by an auto-incrementing `id` and associated with an artifact registration ID. Its fields cover artifact names, creators, creation years, materials, dimensions, weights, cultural periods, geographic origins, and historical significance. It also records acquisition dates and methods, current locations, storage conditions, conservation priorities, display eligibility, insurance values, copyright status, and audit dates.

The data can be used to answer questions such as:
- How many artifacts are recorded by material type, cultural period, or geographic origin?
- Which artifacts were acquired through a given method or during a particular period?
- Which artifacts have a specified conservation priority or storage condition?
- Which artifacts are eligible for permanent or temporary display?
- When were artifacts last audited, and which records may need an audit?
- What insurance values are recorded for artifacts, and how do they vary across categories?

These fields can also support collection inventory, acquisition, display-planning, conservation, and audit analyses.
museum_artifact_large.showcaseenvironmen:
The `ShowcaseEnvironment` table stores environmental monitoring records for museum display cases. Each record includes a showcase identifier and monitoring timestamp, measurements for temperature, humidity, light, UV, CO₂, VOCs, particulate matter, and vibration, along with door-open counts and any triggered alarm. It also records sensor calibration dates, battery levels, data quality flags, emergency contact information, incident response times, responsible staff codes, and notes.

Potential uses include:
- Comparing environmental readings across showcases or over time.
- Identifying records associated with particular alarm types or data quality flags.
- Reviewing door openings, sensor battery levels, and calibration schedules.
- Examining incident response times by showcase, alarm type, or staff member.
- Investigating conditions alongside notes to provide context for readings.

Measurements and several other fields are stored as character strings, so analysis involving numeric comparisons or dates may require converting their values to appropriate types.
museum_artifact_large.artifactcondition:
The `museum_artifact_large.ArtifactCondition` table records condition assessments for museum artifacts. Each record has an ID, an artifact reference, an assessment date, and a staff identifier. Condition fields cover surface integrity, structural stability, color fading, corrosion, crack density, and biological growth. The table also records previous damage, restoration history, recommended conservation actions, urgency, environmental risk, handling cautions, assessment methods and equipment, and links or references for follow-up dates and report attachments.

The table can be used to answer questions such as:

- Which artifacts have severe surface damage, instability, corrosion, or biological growth?
- How many assessments recommend immediate action, restoration, isolation, or expert consultation?
- Which artifacts have high or critical environmental risk, or require special handling?
- How do condition findings change across assessment dates for an artifact?
- Which assessment methods, equipment, or staff are associated with particular findings?
- When are follow-up reviews scheduled, and which assessments document prior damage or restoration?

These records can support analyses of condition patterns, conservation workload and urgency, follow-up scheduling, and the relationship between observed damage and recommended actions.
museum_artifact_large.exhibitionschedule:
The `museum_artifact_large.ExhibitionSchedule` table contains exhibition scheduling records. Each record has an auto-incrementing `id` and an `exhibitionCode` identifier, along with the hall and showcase references, exhibition dates, curator, and theme.

It also records operational and planning details, including projected visitor counts, security levels, climate and lighting requirements, installation and deinstallation dates, insurance coverage, loan agreement references, and marketing budgets. Educational programs, special events, and post-exhibition report references are included as well. These fields are stored as character-varying values.

The records can be used to answer questions such as:
- Which exhibitions are scheduled for a given date range, hall, or curator?
- What security, climate, and lighting requirements are specified for an exhibition?
- How do projected visitor counts or marketing budgets vary across exhibitions?
- Which exhibitions use loan agreements or include educational programs and special events?
- How do installation and deinstallation dates relate to the public exhibition dates?
- Which exhibitions have post-exhibition report references?
museum_artifact_large.artifactloan:
The `museum_artifact_large.ArtifactLoan` table contains records of artifact loans, including the artifact and borrowing institution identifiers, loan dates, purpose, transport and packaging methods, insurance amount, customs status, handling and environmental requirements, security requirements, and legal-document references. It also records return condition, damage documentation, loan fees, approval authority, the staff member managing logistics, and any required follow-up actions.

The table can be used to answer questions such as which artifacts were loaned for a particular purpose or during a given period, which institutions borrowed them, and what transport, packaging, or customs arrangements were used. It can also support analyses of loan durations, fees and insured values, return conditions and reported damage, and the volume of loans managed by staff members.
museum_artifact_large.conservationtreatm:
The `museum_artifact_large.ConservationTreatment` table records conservation treatments performed on artifacts. Each record includes an artifact identifier, treatment date and type, labor duration, materials and equipment used, and the lead and assistant conservator identifiers.

It also stores treatment outcomes and follow-up information, including effectiveness ratings, observed side effects, stability assessments, recommended revisit dates, chemical residue levels, quality-control results, and documentation quality. References to pre- and post-treatment photos, lab conditions, and archive locations are also included.

The data can be used to:
- Count treatments by type, date, artifact, or conservator.
- Compare treatment outcomes, stability, side effects, and quality-control results.
- Review materials, equipment, and labor hours associated with treatments.
- Identify artifacts with revisit recommendations or deteriorating or unstable assessments.
- Assess documentation completeness and the presence of chemical residues.

Dates, durations, and several descriptive fields are stored as character strings, so their formats may need validation before analysis.
museum_artifact_large.researcheraccess:
The `museum_artifact_large.ResearcherAccess` table records researcher access sessions for artifacts. Each record includes a researcher identifier, artifact identifier, access date, research purpose, handling permissions, supervision requirements, and session duration. It also stores information about tools used, samples taken, data collected, publication intent, confidentiality agreements, facility access, emergency procedures, equipment calibration, waste disposal, reported incidents, supervising staff, and approval status.

The table can be used to answer questions such as:
- How many access sessions took place during a given period, or for a particular artifact or researcher?
- What research purposes and handling permissions were associated with sessions?
- Which sessions involved samples, specific tools, or particular facility access levels?
- What were the approval, supervision, confidentiality, or equipment-calibration statuses of sessions?
- How many incidents were reported, and what types of waste-disposal protocols were recorded?

These fields can support analyses of access activity over time, session characteristics, approvals and supervision, sample collection, publication plans, and recorded safety or security incidents.
museum_artifact_large.securityincident:
The `museum_artifact_large.SecurityIncident` table stores security incident records for museum showcases or display areas. Each record includes an incident identifier, showcase ID, incident time, incident type, severity, affected artifacts, alarm response, CCTV availability, responding personnel, response time, containment actions, damage assessment, investigation status, root-cause analysis, corrective measures, regulatory reporting status, insurance claim status, public disclosure approach, lead responder staff code, and lessons learned.

The table can be used to answer questions such as:
- How many incidents occurred by type, severity, or showcase?
- What alarm responses and CCTV coverage were recorded for different incidents?
- How do response times vary across incident types or severity levels?
- Which incidents remain open, in progress, or reopened?
- What damage, containment actions, and corrective measures were recorded?
- How are incidents handled for regulatory reporting, insurance claims, and public disclosure?
- Which staff members were listed as lead responders?

It can also support analyses of incident patterns by showcase or type, response and containment practices, investigation status, and recorded outcomes. The schema describes incident times and response times as character fields, so calculations involving time may require interpreting those values.
museum_artifact_large.materialanalysislo:
The `museum_artifact_large.MaterialAnalysisLog` table records material analyses performed on museum artifacts. Each record includes the analysis date and method, identified composition and structure, elemental results, aging indicators, degradation products, contamination findings, and the artifact location and sample size. It also stores information about invasiveness, equipment calibration, laboratory conditions, technician notes, peer review, data retention, and the reference to raw analytical data.

The `surfaceReadingId` links an analysis to a surface-condition baseline, and `staffCode` identifies the analyzing conservator. The table could be used to:

- Review analyses by date, method, conservator, or artifact location.
- Examine recorded aging indicators, degradation products, and contamination findings.
- Compare results across analytical methods or linked surface readings.
- Check peer-review status, equipment calibration, and data-retention requirements.
- Identify analyses by sample size or non-invasive score.
museum_artifact_large.transportationmoni:
The `museum_artifact_large.TransportationMonitor` table records transport details for artifacts. Each row has an auto-incrementing ID and identifies a shipment batch and artifact, along with departure and arrival times, carrier, vehicle type, route, and logistics coordinator.

The table also includes transit-condition and handling fields: minimum and maximum temperature and humidity, shock-event count, GPS accuracy, customs delay, and number of handling transfers. Arrival packaging condition, receiver verification result, and anomaly reports record delivery outcomes and protocol deviations.

The table can be used to answer questions such as:
- Which vehicle types or carriers were used for artifact shipments?
- What packaging conditions or verification results were recorded on arrival?
- Which shipments had reported anomalies, shock events, customs delays, or multiple transfers?
- How did recorded environmental conditions vary across shipments?
- How do shipment outcomes vary by carrier, vehicle type, route, or logistics coordinator?

Several measurement and count fields are defined as character strings, so they may need conversion before numeric analysis.
museum_artifact_large.lightradiationlog:
The `museum_artifact_large.LightRadiationLog` table records light and radiation measurements for museum showcases or display areas. Each record has an ID and a reference to a base radiation reading, along with the showcase identifier and measurement timestamp.

Measurements include visible light in lux; UV-A, UV-B, and infrared radiation; blue-light index; and cumulative exposure. The table also records lighting and monitoring details, such as light source type, filter status, distance to the artifact, beam angle, color temperature, CRI, flicker percentage, sensor position, and maintenance notes. A staff code identifies the associated lighting specialist.

The data can be used to compare light and radiation conditions across showcases or over time, examine exposure levels in relation to filter status or light source, identify records associated with maintenance activity, and analyze measurements by sensor position or staff member. These fields can also support questions about how lighting conditions and cumulative exposure vary by display area. Numeric measurements and timestamps are stored as character-varying fields, so analysis may require converting them to appropriate data types.
museum_artifact_large.digitalassetlink:
The `DigitalAssetLink` table records links between digital assets and the physical artifacts they represent. It includes asset and artifact identifiers, file format, image specifications, capture date, photographer, lighting and background details, metadata completeness, copyright and usage rights, storage and backup locations, access frequency, verification date, migration plan, AI-tagging confidence, and permission for public display.

The table can support questions and analyses such as:
- How many linked assets use each file format, color depth, or capture setup?
- Which assets are permitted for public display, and under what restrictions?
- Which files have incomplete metadata or have not been verified recently?
- How are assets distributed across storage locations and access-frequency categories?
- Which assets have documented migration plans or AI-tagging confidence values?
- What digital assets are associated with a particular physical artifact?
museum_artifact_large.publicationrecord:
The `museum_artifact_large.PublicationRecord` table stores publication metadata. Each record has an auto-incrementing ID and a publication code, along with the title, publication year, publisher, ISBN or ISSN, language, page count, and cover type.

It also records distribution and access details, including distribution channel, print run, digital availability, open-access status, licensing terms, and copyright holder. Additional fields cover citation count, impact factor, peer-review type, editorial board, and archival location.

The table can be used to answer questions such as:
- How many publications were released in a given year or by a particular publisher?
- What languages, formats, or distribution channels are represented?
- Which publications are open access, digitally available, or under specific licensing terms?
- How do citation counts or impact factors vary across publications?
- Where are publications archived, and who holds their copyright?
- What are the publication’s page count, print run, and peer-review type?
museum_artifact_large.airqualitymonitor:
The `AirQualityMonitor` table stores air-quality measurements for museum showcases or display areas. Each record includes a reading reference, showcase identifier, measurement timestamp, concentrations of particulate matter and gases, air exchange rate, filter efficiency, sensor calibration and maintenance dates, anomaly status, corrective actions, and the staff code associated with the record.

The data can be used to:

- Review pollutant measurements by showcase and over time.
- Identify readings associated with anomalies such as spikes, drift, sensor failure, or contamination.
- Compare air exchange rates and filter efficiency with recorded pollutant levels.
- Track sensor calibration and upcoming maintenance dates.
- Examine corrective actions and relate them to subsequent measurements.
- Compare monitoring records across staff members using `staffCode`.

Many measurement, date, and status fields are stored as character-varying values, so analysis may require converting them to numeric or date types.
museum_artifact_large.riskassessmentdeta:
The `museum_artifact_large.RiskAssessmentDetail` table stores risk assessment records linked to baseline condition assessments and staff assessors. Each record can include the assessment date, risk category, likelihood and impact scores, overall and residual risk levels, vulnerability factors, threat sources, mitigation measures, estimated implementation cost and timeline, review frequency, monitoring indicators, contingency plans, stakeholder notification protocol, regulatory compliance status, and a report reference.

The table can be used to answer questions such as:
- Which risk categories or artifacts have the highest likelihood, impact, or risk level?
- What mitigation measures, costs, and timelines are associated with identified risks?
- How do residual risk levels compare with initial risk levels?
- Which assessments have major compliance gaps or require specific stakeholder notifications?
- How do risks and mitigation progress vary by assessment date, assessor, or condition assessment?

Possible analyses include summarizing risk levels by category or period, comparing likelihood and impact scores, tracking mitigation costs and timelines, identifying recurring vulnerability factors or threat sources, and reviewing reassessment schedules.
museum_artifact_large.insurancepolicydet:
The `museum_artifact_large.InsurancePolicyDetail` table stores insurance policy records associated with artifacts. Each record includes an artifact identifier, contract number, insurer, coverage dates, coverage scope, insured value, premium, deductible, exclusions, claims history, appraisal details, renewal reminder, broker contact, special conditions, staff coordinator, and a reference to the policy document. It also includes a risk assessment reference.

The table can be used to answer questions such as which artifacts are insured, which insurer covers an artifact, when a policy starts or expires, and what coverage limits, premiums, and deductibles apply. It can support analyses of coverage by peril type, upcoming renewals, differences between appraisal and insured values, claim history, and policy details by insurer or staff coordinator.
museum_artifact_large.corporatesponsorre:
The `museum_artifact_large.CorporateSponsorRecord` table contains corporate sponsorship records, including sponsor and company identifiers, sponsorship type and amount, currency, agreement dates, payment schedule, and contract details. It also records sponsor benefits, logo placement, naming rights, media mentions, tax deduction status, renewal likelihood, satisfaction scores, relationship managers, upcoming engagement dates, and public acknowledgment methods.

The records can be used to summarize sponsorships by company, type, amount, or currency; track agreement terms and payment schedules; review benefits and recognition provided; and monitor sponsor satisfaction, renewal likelihood, and upcoming engagement activities. Date and contract fields may also support analysis of sponsorship duration, execution timing, and renewal planning. Because several fields are stored as character varying, analyses involving amounts, dates, counts, or scores may require parsing or standardization.
museum_artifact_large.emergencyresponsel:
The `museum_artifact_large.EmergencyResponseLog` table records emergency responses linked to security incidents through `incidentId`. Each record includes the response timestamp, team, actions taken, resources deployed, personnel count, evacuation status, and any external agencies involved. It also captures communications, damage-control measures, artifact recovery and stabilization, evidence preservation, media handling, regulatory notifications, timeline accuracy, documented lessons, and recommended drill frequency. Lead and support staff codes identify the response commanders.

The table can be used to:
- Review response actions, staffing, resources, and evacuation status by incident or response team.
- Analyze response timelines and the accuracy of incident reconstructions.
- Track artifact recovery, damage-control measures, and evidence-preservation outcomes.
- Examine external-agency involvement and communication, media, and regulatory-notification practices.
- Summarize lessons documented and recommended drill frequencies to inform emergency planning.
museum_artifact_large.artifactusagelog:
The `museum_artifact_large.ArtifactUsageLog` table records artifact handling and usage sessions. Each record includes the usage date and type, requesting department and purpose, time outside secure storage, environmental exposure, physical stress level, and artifact condition before and after use. It also stores conservation review status, approval authority, supervision level, equipment and safety measures, incidents, follow-up actions, staff identifier, and a reference to the session report.

The `usageRecordId` links a log entry to a usage requirements profile, while `staffCode` links it to a staff record.

The table can be used to analyze usage by date, purpose, department, or artifact-related requirements; compare pre- and post-use condition; review incidents and follow-up actions; track conservation reviews; and examine handling duration, stress levels, supervision, or environmental exposure across sessions.
museum_artifact_large.conservationmainte:
The `museum_artifact_large.ConservationMaintenanceLog` table records conservation and maintenance activities. Each record includes a maintenance reference, activity date and type, tasks performed, materials and equipment used, and labor duration. It also stores pre- and post-maintenance photo references, effectiveness ratings, issues encountered, environmental conditions, waste generated, and safety incidents.

The table tracks follow-up and verification details, including the next scheduled maintenance date, quality-check result, documentation status, the performing staff member, and a maintenance report reference. The maintenance record links to `ConservationAndMaintenance` through `maintenanceId`, and the staff member links to `Staff` through `staffCode`.

Possible uses include reviewing maintenance history by activity type, date, or staff member; examining reported issues and safety incidents; assessing effectiveness ratings and quality-check outcomes; comparing labor duration or materials used across activities; and identifying records with pending follow-up, incomplete documentation, or a future scheduled date. Dates and duration are stored as character-varying values, so analysis may require parsing or standardizing them.
organ_transplant_large.demographics:
The `organ_transplant_large.demographics` table stores donor demographic and physical information. Each donor is identified by `contrib_registry`, the primary key. The table includes age, ABO blood type, country or nationality reference, and a JSON field containing physical measurements and characteristics such as height, weight, and BMI.

The data can be used to answer questions about donors by age, blood type, or country; review physical characteristics; and analyze how donor demographics and measurements vary across groups.
organ_transplant_large.recipients_immuno:
The `organ_transplant_large.recipients_immunology` table stores immunological data linked to recipient demographics through `immu_recip_registry`. It includes PRA scores, donor-specific antibody status, crossmatch results, CMV and EBV status, functional status, life-support requirements, and HLA typing profiles for A, B, DR, and DQ. A `NULL` value for `life_support` means the status is not applicable or not documented.

The data can be used to examine recipient sensitization and compatibility indicators, such as PRA scores, antibody status, crossmatch results, and HLA profiles. It can also answer questions about the distribution of infection statuses, functional assessments, and documented life-support requirements among recipients.
organ_transplant_large.administrative_an:
The `organ_transplant_large.administrative_and_review` table contains administrative and review information linked to transplant matching records through `adm_rev_registry`. It records expert review, ethics committee approval, regulatory compliance, documentation, consent, financial clearance, and insurance approval statuses, along with expert review notes. It also includes references to coordinators, surgeons, transplant and recovery centers, laboratories, donors, and recipients.

Status and notes values may contain inconsistent capitalization. For the review and approval fields, `NULL` indicates that the corresponding review or approval is pending, incomplete, or not applicable, as specified for each field.

The table can be used to:
- Count records by review, approval, compliance, documentation, consent, or clearance status.
- Identify records with pending or incomplete administrative reviews.
- Examine expert review notes alongside review outcomes.
- Group administrative records by coordinator, surgeon, center, or laboratory.
- Link administrative review information to donor and recipient records.
organ_transplant_large.complications:
The `organ_transplant_large.complications` table stores records describing transplant-related medical complications. Each record has a unique `complication_registry` identifier and fields for the complication’s name, medical code, and category. The listed complication types include rejection, infection, cardiovascular and bone disease, graft nephropathy, lymphoproliferative disorder, and surgical site infection.

Additional fields describe associated risk factors and symptoms; diagnosis methods; treatment options and prevention measures; prognosis and long-term effects; regulatory reporting requirements; and research notes. The `severityriskprofile` JSONB field is intended to hold severity and risk information, including mortality risk, impact scores, and timeline information. `diagnosis_method` may be null when the method is unspecified, and `research_notes` may be null when no research documentation is present. `last_updated` records the date and time of the record’s last update.

The table can support analyses and questions such as:
- Which complications are associated with particular risk factors or symptoms?
- What diagnosis, treatment, or prevention approaches are listed for a given complication?
- How do prognosis and long-term effects vary by complication type?
- Which records require regulatory reporting or have research notes?
- How are severity and risk profiles represented across complications?
- When were complication records last updated?
organ_transplant_large.quality_metrics:
`organ_transplant_large.quality_metrics` stores quality metric definitions and monitoring information for organ transplant care. Each record is identified by `metric_registry` and includes a metric’s name, category, measurement type, data source, benchmark source, national average, trend direction, responsible department, review committee, and last-updated timestamp. It may also include an action requirement, notes, and JSON configuration for thresholds and measurement parameters. A `NULL` data source means it was not specified; a `NULL` benchmark means one is unavailable; and a `NULL` action or notes field indicates none is recorded.

The listed metrics cover survival, readmissions, acute rejection, length of stay, medication adherence, and surgical site infections. The table can be used to compare metric values with national averages, review trends and thresholds, identify metrics flagged for action, and group metrics by category, department, committee, or data source. It can also support analyses of which metrics lack specified sources or benchmarks and when metric records were last updated.
organ_transplant_large.equipment:
The `organ_transplant_large.equipment` table records medical equipment, with one row per equipment registry identifier. It contains equipment names and types, model and serial numbers, manufacturers, purchase and installation dates, facility locations and hospital references, operational status, safety certifications, usage hours, replacement costs, and maintenance and service information stored as JSON.

The table can support questions and analyses such as:
- Which equipment is operational or under maintenance, and where is it located?
- What equipment is installed at each hospital?
- How are equipment types, manufacturers, and replacement costs distributed?
- Which records have no purchase date recorded?
- How do usage hours relate to operational status or maintenance history?
- What scheduled maintenance, service dates, or warranty information is recorded?
organ_transplant_large.team_training_par:
The `organ_transplant_large.team_training_participation` table records medical teams’ participation in training programs. Each record has a unique participation identifier and references a team and training program. It includes registration and completion dates, participation status, attendance rate, assessment score, and skill demonstration.

The table also records certification details, including the certification earned and its date and expiry, along with training effectiveness, knowledge improvement, implementation plans, follow-up requirements, continuing education credits, cost center, feedback score, and recommendations. NULL values indicate when specified outcomes or evaluations have not occurred or were not provided, as described in the schema.

The data can be used to answer questions such as:
- Which teams registered for or completed particular training programs, and when?
- Which participants are still in progress or have withdrawn?
- What are attendance, assessment, and skill-demonstration outcomes?
- Which certifications were earned, and when do they expire?
- How do effectiveness, knowledge improvement, and feedback scores vary across training programs?
- How many continuing education credits were earned, and which cost centers were charged?
- What follow-up or implementation plans are recorded for completed training?
organ_transplant_large.organ_banks:
The `organ_transplant_large.organ_banks` table stores organ bank records. Each record has a unique registry identifier and includes the bank’s name, type, license and accreditation details, and a reference to an associated hospital.

The table also records storage capacity and current inventory, organ types stored, preservation methods and equipment, backup systems, quality-control procedures, staff qualifications, operating schedules, emergency response times, and transplant coordination. Research capabilities, compliance status, and annual processing volume are included as well. A `NULL` value indicates that certain information—such as a license number, inventory, accreditation, coordination procedures, or research capabilities—is not recorded or specified, as described in the schema.

The data can be used to:
- Compare banks by type, storage capacity, inventory, or annual volume.
- Identify facilities that store particular organ types or use specific preservation methods.
- Review operating schedules, emergency procedures, and backup systems.
- Examine compliance status, accreditation, and staff qualifications.
- Link organ banks to associated hospitals and assess where information is missing.
organ_transplant_large.consent_forms:
The `organ_transplant_large.consent_forms` table stores consent form records. Each record has a unique `consent_registry` identifier and may reference a patient and a donor. Form details include the form type, version, consent category, language, signing date and time, witness information, and whether an interpreter was used.

The table also records consent status, withdrawal and expiration dates, signature information, document location, compliance verification, and notes. A `NULL` value has field-specific meaning: for example, it can indicate that no legal guardian or interpreter was involved, a witness signature or digital signature was not required or used, or consent was not withdrawn or does not expire.

The data can support questions and analyses such as:
- How many forms exist by form type, consent category, language, or status?
- Which forms are withdrawn, and when were they withdrawn?
- Which active forms have expiration dates approaching?
- How often were interpreters or legal guardians involved?
- How are consent records associated with patient and donor references?
- Which forms have compliance verification or recorded signature details?
organ_transplant_large.support_groups:
The `organ_transplant_large.support_groups` table contains support group details, identified by a group registry ID. Its fields describe each group’s name and type, target population, meeting schedule, location and format, facilitator and credentials, capacity and current membership, registration requirements, cost, language, accessibility features, discussion topics, resources, contact information, referral source, and outcomes tracked.

The table can be used to answer questions such as:
- Which groups serve a particular population or cover a particular topic?
- When and where do groups meet, and are they in-person, virtual, or hybrid?
- Which groups require registration, charge a cost, or provide specific accessibility features?
- Which groups have a facilitator assigned, and what credentials are recorded?
- How do current membership counts compare with group capacity?
- What resources and outcomes are associated with each group?

Null values indicate that the corresponding information is not specified or, for membership counts, is not tracked.
organ_transplant_large.recipients_demogr:
The `organ_transplant_large.recipients_demographics` table contains one record per transplant recipient, identified by `recip_registry`. It includes demographic and physical measurements recorded at transplant evaluation: age, gender classification, ABO blood type, height, weight, BMI, and ethnic or racial background.

The data can be used to summarize recipient characteristics, compare age or physical measurements across demographic groups, examine the distribution of blood types, and analyze how recipient demographics vary across the recorded ethnic or racial classifications.
organ_transplant_large.transplant_matchi:
The `organ_transplant_large.transplant_matching` table contains records of donor–recipient matching processes for heart, kidney, liver, lung, and pancreas transplants. Each record includes references to the donor and recipient, the organ type, match status, compatibility level and score, confidence and decision-support scores, algorithm version, matching run identifier, and timestamps and duration for the process.

The table can be used to answer questions such as:
- How many matching records exist for each organ type or status?
- How do match scores, confidence values, and decision-support scores vary by organ or compatibility level?
- How long do matching processes take, and how does duration vary by status, organ, or algorithm version?
- How do matching outcomes differ across runs or over time?
- Which records are associated with particular donors or recipients?
organ_transplant_large.data_source_and_q:
The `organ_transplant_large.data_source_and_quality` table links data quality information to a transplant matching record through `q_match_registry`. It contains the reported data source, data quality and completeness scores, verification status, last-update timestamp, scheduled review date, and references to donor and recipient demographic records.

`data_src_val` and `verif_stat_val` may have inconsistent capitalization. A `NULL` data source indicates that its information is undocumented or unknown; a `NULL` verification status indicates verification is pending or was not performed. Update dates use `yyyy/mm/dd`, while review dates use `dd/mm/yyyy`, so date values may need parsing into a consistent format for analysis.

The table can be used to examine quality and completeness scores across matching records, identify records with missing source information or pending verification, and review update and validation schedules. Its donor and recipient references can also support comparisons of quality assessments across related demographic records.
organ_transplant_large.medical_history:
The `organ_transplant_large.medical_history` table stores donor medical-history and screening information. Each row is identified by `contrib_med_registry`, which links to a donor demographics record. Fields include recorded medical conditions, smoking status and history, alcohol and drug use, and viral test results for CMV, EBV, HBV, HCV, and HIV.

A `NULL` value in `med_history` indicates that medical-history documentation is incomplete or unavailable. A `NULL` in `alc_cond` or `drug_cond` indicates that the corresponding history was not documented or assessed.

The table can be used to:
- Review donors’ recorded medical conditions and substance-use histories.
- Summarize smoking, alcohol, or drug-use status across donor records.
- Examine viral screening results by infection or donor.
- Identify records with missing medical-history or substance-use documentation.
- Compare screening and history data with donor demographics through `contrib_med_registry`.
organ_transplant_large.compatibility_met:
`organ_transplant_large.compatibility_metrics` contains compatibility and logistics information for donor-recipient transplant matches. Each row is keyed by `match_comp_registry`, which links to a transplant matching record. Donor and recipient reference fields support linking to their respective demographic records.

The data includes the HLA mismatch count, blood compatibility assessment, estimated geographic distance, expected cold ischemia and transport times, estimated cost, and a JSON object containing HLA, size, and age compatibility scores. The schema lists `0` as a possible HLA mismatch count. Blood compatibility values may have inconsistent capitalization, and a `NULL` value means the assessment is pending or unavailable. Distance, time, and cost are stored as text, with examples that include units or currency formatting.

The table can be used to:
- Review compatibility and logistics metrics for individual matches.
- Compare matches by blood compatibility, HLA mismatch count, or compatibility scores.
- Analyze estimated travel distance, transport time, ischemia time, and cost across matches.
- Join matching metrics to donor and recipient demographic records for grouped analysis.
organ_transplant_large.protocols:
The `organ_transplant_large.protocols` table stores transplant-related medical protocols, with one record identified by `protocol_registry`. Fields describe each protocol’s name, version, type, specialty, target condition, evidence level, approval and lifecycle dates, authoring organization, guideline source, compliance and training requirements, quality and outcome measures, cost-effectiveness, implementation notes, and related protocols.

The date fields are stored as text. A `NULL` evidence level means it has not been assessed; a `NULL` review date means no review is scheduled; and a `NULL` related-protocols value means none have been identified.

The table can be used to look up protocols by specialty or condition, track approval, effective, review, and expiration dates, compare evidence levels and requirements, examine stated quality and outcome measures, review cost-effectiveness values, and identify related protocols or implementation requirements.
organ_transplant_large.hospitals:
The `organ_transplant_large.hospitals` table contains one record per hospital, identified by a unique registry ID. It includes each facility’s name and type, accreditation status, bed and ICU capacity, operating room count, trauma designation, teaching status, research funding, emergency service volume, and a JSON field with address and contact information.

The data can support questions and analyses such as:
- How many hospitals have a given facility type or trauma designation?
- How do bed, ICU, and operating room capacities vary across hospitals?
- Which hospitals have designated teaching status or reported research funding?
- What emergency patient volumes are reported by facility?
- Where are hospitals located, and how can they be contacted?
organ_transplant_large.hla_info:
The `organ_transplant_large.hla_info` table contains donor HLA antigen typing values for HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-DR, and HLA-DQ. Each row is linked to donor demographics through `immu_don_registry`, which is the table’s primary key and a foreign key to the demographics table.

The data can be used to examine donor HLA typing patterns, compare antigen values across donors, and join HLA information with demographic data. It can also support analyses of donor compatibility characteristics based on the recorded HLA values.
organ_transplant_large.risk_evaluation:
The `organ_transplant_large.risk_evaluation` table stores transplant risk evaluation records, keyed by `risk_eval_registry`, which links each record to a transplant matching record. It includes scores for organ quality, expected graft and patient survival, surgical complexity and risk, resource availability, transplant center experience, volume and outcomes, quality of life, cost effectiveness, and allocation priority.

The table also contains references to donor and recipient demographic records, a `riskmetrics` JSON field covering immunological, infection, rejection, complication, readmission, and mortality risks, and text fields for cost per QALY, resource consumption, and staff time. A NULL `surg_risk_val` may indicate an incomplete or unperformed assessment, but some NULLs were randomly added as data noise. A NULL `qol_val` indicates that the assessment is incomplete or unavailable.

The data can be used to compare risk and survival scores across transplant matching records, examine how center characteristics relate to evaluation scores, analyze allocation priorities, and assess recorded costs, resource use, and staff requirements.
organ_transplant_large.training_programs:
The `organ_transplant_large.training_programs` table stores records describing organ-transplant training programs. Each record has a unique `training_registry` identifier and may include the program’s name and type, training category, intended audience, duration, format, delivery method, prerequisites, learning objectives, curriculum, assessment method, certification, continuing-education credits, cost, instructor credentials, participant limit, schedule, location, and materials provided.

The table can support questions and analyses such as:
- Which programs serve a particular audience or training category?
- How do programs differ in duration, delivery method, format, or schedule?
- Which programs offer a particular certification or continuing-education credits?
- What prerequisites, assessment methods, or learning objectives are associated with each program?
- How many programs have specified costs, schedules, formats, or instructor credentials?

A `NULL` value means that the corresponding detail is not specified, no prerequisites are required, no continuing-education credits are offered, or the schedule is not finalized, according to the field’s definition.
organ_transplant_large.surgeons:
The `organ_transplant_large.surgeons` table stores surgeon-level records, identified by `surgeon_registry`. It includes names, titles, license numbers, specialties and subspecialties, education, experience, board certifications, languages, contact details, practice start dates, retirement dates, current status, case success rates, publication counts, and teaching positions.

A `NULL` value indicates that the relevant information is unspecified or unavailable, or—in the case of retirement date—that retirement is not planned or the surgeon is active, as described in the schema.

The table can be used to answer questions such as:
- Which surgeons specialize in a particular transplant area?
- Which surgeons are active or on leave, or have a planned retirement date?
- How do surgeons compare by experience, board certifications, or case success rate?
- Which surgeons speak a particular language or hold a teaching position?
- How many surgeons have recorded contact, certification, or subspecialty information?
- How do publication counts or experience vary across specialties?
organ_transplant_large.medical_teams:
The `organ_transplant_large.medical_teams` table stores medical team records. Each record has a unique `team_registry` identifier and includes the team’s name, type, specialty area, associated hospital, leader identifier, formation date, and operational status.

Additional fields describe team size, collective experience, success rate, annual case volume, certification level, research involvement, training level, quality score, contact information, availability hours, and notes. The schema indicates that some fields may be `NULL` when information is unavailable or has not been recorded, such as team leadership, formation date, performance metrics, research activities, and contact details.

The table can be used to:
- List teams by specialty, type, hospital, or active status.
- Compare teams by size, experience, annual case volume, success rate, or quality score.
- Review team certifications, training levels, and research involvement.
- Identify teams with missing leadership, performance, contact, or formation information.
- Summarize team availability and contact details.
organ_transplant_large.transportation:
The `organ_transplant_large.transportation` table stores organ-transport operation records. Each record has a unique transport registry identifier and includes the transport method, vehicle, route, origin and destination hospitals, and operational status. It also records assigned driver information, required equipment, medical escort, temperature-control requirements, and security level. A null driver indicates that no driver is assigned; a null temperature-control value indicates that no temperature control is needed. The `transitmetrics` JSONB field contains logistics information such as timing, environmental conditions, and cost or distance metrics.

The table can be used to:
- Track transports by status, method, vehicle, route, or hospital.
- Identify transports without an assigned driver or with specific equipment, escort, temperature, or security requirements.
- Analyze routes, transport times, environmental conditions, costs, and distances using the transit metrics.
- Compare transport operations across origin and destination hospitals.
organ_transplant_large.surgeon_hospital_:
The `organ_transplant_large.surgeon_hospital_affiliations` table stores surgeon-to-hospital affiliation records. Each record has a unique `affiliation_registry` identifier and references a surgeon and a hospital. It includes affiliation type, start and end dates, primary-affiliation designation, status, department, position title, and privileges level.

Additional fields describe annual case volume, quality metrics, teaching and research involvement, committee memberships, contact extension, office location, administrative role, and notes. A `NULL` end date indicates an ongoing affiliation. `NULL` values in case volume, quality metrics, teaching, research, committee memberships, contact extension, or administrative role have the meanings specified in the schema.

The table can be used to identify which hospitals surgeons are affiliated with, distinguish primary from other affiliations, review affiliation status and dates, and compare surgeons’ roles and privileges across hospitals. It can also support analyses of case volumes, recorded quality metrics, teaching and research activities, committee participation, and administrative responsibilities by surgeon, hospital, or department.
organ_transplant_large.rehabilitation_pr:
The `organ_transplant_large.rehabilitation_programs` table contains rehabilitation program records, identified by `rehab_registry` values such as RH001–RH007. It describes each program’s name and type, target population, duration and session schedule, clinical team, treatment modalities, goals, outcome measures, required equipment, and location.

The table also includes costs per session, insurance coverage, eligibility criteria, referral processes, success rates, patient satisfaction scores, and quality indicators. A `NULL` value indicates that the relevant information is not specified, established, or measured, depending on the column.

The data can be used to compare programs by population served, treatment approach, setting, staffing, schedule, cost, or coverage. It can also support analysis of which outcome measures and quality indicators are used, identification of programs matching particular eligibility or referral criteria, and review of reported success rates and satisfaction scores. These comparisons should account for missing values in the relevant fields.
organ_transplant_large.tissue_samples:
The `organ_transplant_large.tissue_samples` table records tissue sample details. Each record is identified by `sample_registry`, and `donor_ref` links the sample to a donor demographics record.

Fields cover sample type, collection date and time, collection method, size, storage location and temperature, preservation method, quality grade, contamination status, viability score, expiration date, processing status, laboratory results, pathology findings, research-use consent, chain-of-custody reference, and notes. Date and time values are stored as text. A `NULL` value indicates that collection time was not recorded, contamination was not assessed, no expiration date was set, research consent was not obtained, or no notes were recorded, depending on the field.

The table can support questions and analyses such as:
- How many samples are recorded by type, donor, collection method, or processing status?
- Which samples have a given quality grade, contamination status, or viability score?
- How are samples distributed across storage locations and preservation methods?
- Which samples have pending processing, an upcoming expiration date, or no expiration date?
- How do laboratory results and pathology findings vary by sample type or collection method?
- What proportion of samples have research-use consent recorded or contamination status assessed?
organ_transplant_large.function_and_reco:
The `organ_transplant_large.function_and_recovery` table contains donor organ recovery, preservation, and function data. `recov_don_registry` links each record to donor demographics. Other fields include donor serum creatinine and GFR, cause of death, organ recovery date and time, preservation method, and cold ischemia time. The `organfuncassess` JSONB field groups liver, cardiac, and pulmonary function assessments.

The data can be used to examine donor kidney-function measures, compare recovery and preservation details, analyze cold ischemia times, and review function assessments across organ types. It can also support questions about how these characteristics vary by donor cause of death or be joined with donor demographic data. Dates, measurements, and other fields are stored as text, so their formats may need to be standardized for analysis.
organ_transplant_large.allocation_detail:
The `organ_transplant_large.allocation_details` table records allocation details linked to transplant matching records. Each row is identified by `allc_match_registry` and includes an allocation sequence number, region, policy version, and references to donor and recipient demographic records.

The table can be used to examine allocation rankings by region or policy version, identify the donor and recipient records associated with a match, and count or compare allocation records across regions, sequence numbers, or policy versions.
organ_transplant_large.clinical:
The `organ_transplant_large.clinical` table contains recipient-level clinical information linked to recipient demographics through `clin_recip_registry`. Fields cover the primary diagnosis, waiting-list time, medical urgency, number of previous transplants, dialysis status and duration, and comorbid conditions.

Potential uses include analyzing waiting times by diagnosis or urgency, comparing clinical characteristics across transplant recipients, examining patterns in dialysis treatment and comorbidities, and assessing how prior transplants relate to clinical status. The urgency values include both numbered and `Status`-prefixed forms, so the values `2`, `3`, and similar entries may need normalization before grouping. Null dialysis and comorbidity fields indicate information that is not applicable, undocumented, or unavailable, as specified in the schema.
organ_transplant_large.logistics:
